A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChatQA 2 and provide readable methods, experiments, tables and figures. All pages were inspected, including v2's new Appendix A; v1 ends with references and has no appendix. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ChatQA-2-70B benchmark results, retrieval ablations and a Needle in a Haystack evaluation.

after.justification: v2 reports original ChatQA-2-70B and 8B evaluations, retrieval analyses and comparative needle/passkey experiments, including Appendix A.

M1.justification: The documented method retains the same context-extension recipe, RoPE adjustment, three-stage instruction tuning, synthetic NarrativeQA construction and E5-mistral retrieval. The added 8B configuration does not introduce a different algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: The training datasets and four InfiniteBench, six 32K and nine ChatRAG evaluation tasks remain unchanged. Synthetic coverage expands from v1's single generically described needle test to separately reported natural-language fact and numeric-passkey scenarios in v2 Figures 1 and 3; v1 does not specify its exact needle.

E2.justification: v2 adds Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama3.1-70B-Instruct across all three benchmark groups and as needle/passkey comparators. Kimi-Chat disappears from the InfiniteBench comparison. GPT-4-1106 preview loses its Table 2 row, although its aggregate result remains quoted in Section 5.2.

E3.justification: v2 adds 8B model configurations and changes the selected ChatQA-2 retrieval setting for the beyond-100K comparison from top-5 to top-30 chunks (v1 Table 6 versus v2 Table 5). Main benchmark metrics, dataset exclusions and default top-5 retrieval with 1200-token chunks remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled comparison of natural-language needle and numeric-passkey difficulty across ChatQA 2 and Llama3.1. Chunk-size and retrieval-budget ablations already existed in v1 Tables 1 and 5; v2 revises their presentation and evidence in Figure 2, omitting the previous 32K top-30 endpoint.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional heatmaps show performance across test conditions, not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: In Tables 2-4, reported ChatQA-2-70B averages change from 34.11 to 41.04 on InfiniteBench, 47.37 to 48.15 on 32K tasks, and 54.81 to 56.30 on ChatRAG. Qwen2's InfiniteBench average changes from 34.88 to 39.77. v2 adds 8B/Llama3.1 results and reverses the reported 32K RAG-versus-full-context trend. The beyond-100K RAG comparison also changes retrieval budgets, so its higher score is not a same-setting gain.

T1.justification: Neither version presents new formal theory or proofs. The descriptive RoPE discussion and method reasoning are retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: v1 claims approximately GPT-4-Turbo-level long-context performance and that direct long-context use beats RAG on 32K tasks. v2 claims superiority over GPT-4-Turbo, Qwen2 and Llama3.1 on beyond-100K and short-context RAG benchmarks, and that sufficiently large retrieval sets outperform direct context on both 32K and 128K tasks. Public release of research resources also becomes an explicit contribution.

C2.justification: The practical interpretation of 32K retrieval changes from an accuracy sacrifice for efficiency to an accuracy advantage with sufficient retrieved text. v2 emphasizes robustness to chunk size rather than v1's preference for larger chunks, identifies passkey retrieval as an easier diagnostic, and newly attributes weak summarization to insufficient summarization SFT data.

D1.justification: v2 newly announces released model weights, training data and evaluation setup, and supplies a project access address, materially expanding documented reproducibility access beyond v1's recipe and source-dataset links. It also specifies the needle texts and passkey question. Core training hyperparameters remain unchanged; the external resources themselves were not inspected.

R1.justification: v2 discusses concurrent Llama3.1 models and positions ChatQA 2's released training data and reproduction recipe against Qwen2/Llama3.1's open-weight availability. The broader related-work survey and bibliography are substantially retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements are rewritten, three existing method sections become subsections of Method, and RAG-versus-long-context analysis becomes a standalone section. Context-length terminology and author text also change. Most underlying technical exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds an illustrated overview table, replaces the earlier retrieval-ablation tables with Figure 2, expands the main needle figure into four panels, and adds four appendix passkey panels. Benchmark tables are expanded and regrouped, alongside a changed document template. These substantially alter the paper's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the evaluation more informative through Llama3.1 comparisons, 8B results and explicit fact-versus-passkey diagnostics, while newly documenting resource access. The benefit is limited by unreconciled evidence: Figure 2 places the full-context reference near 47.9 whereas Table 3 reports 48.15, and substantial score revisions lack corresponding explanations in the largely unchanged training recipe. The added comparisons improve usefulness, but the higher reported scores alone do not establish stronger paper quality.
